message.content: I have full context: single-workload softmax-attention kernel with an fp16 round-trip on the probabilities and a structured value offset engineered to create cancellation in the output. I'll record the description model now.

function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["Single fixed workload: make_inputs() in kernel.py, seed 815, n=128, d=32, attention family; no other inputs/shapes in scope.", "Contract op: y = softmax(K @ q / sqrt(D)) @ V with softmax over N=128 tokens; output is d=32 vector.", "Reference computed in float64 from the exact same float32 input values; tolerance E = ||out-ref||_2 / max(||ref||_2, 0.001*sqrt(32)) must be <= 0.001, all outputs finite.", "Reduced precision / approximate arithmetic is explicitly permitted if the budget is met; verdict options are trust / reject / needs_more_evidence and scope is finite-workload only.", "Inputs are generated on CPU (NumPy PCG64), rounded once to binary32 before transfer; k is scaled by 1.9 (tail-heavier scores) and v is offset by 0.5*(p@v) to deliberately control output cancellation magnitude."], "kernel_model": ["Triton single-program kernel (_kernel) with grid (1,), loads full K (128x32) and V (128x32) tiles, computes scores = row-dot(k, q) * D^-0.5 in input (fp32) precision.", "Softmax computed as exp(scores - max(scores)) then normalized by the sum; result p is then cast to fp16 and back to fp32 (line 15) — a lossy quantization of the probabilities before the value-weighted sum.", "Output y = sum(p[:,None]*v, 0), stored as float32; run() allocates a d-sized fp32 output and launches with enable_fp_fusion=False.", "run() derives N and D from k.shape so it matches the workload shapes; no masking needed since N=128 and D=32 exactly tile the ranges.", "make_inputs deliberately constructs v such that v -= 0.5 * (p @ v), shrinking the reference output norm (p@v with new v is 0.5 of the original), which lowers the denominator of E and makes fp16 probability error relatively larger."], "risk_map": ["fp16 quantization of softmax probabilities (line 15): each p_i rounds to ~1e-3 relative error, and since y is a convex combination of V rows, the perturbation in y is roughly sum(|p_err_i| * |v_i|), which scales like ||V|| * eps_fp16 * sqrt-ish factor — with the shrunken reference norm (v offset by 0.5*(p@v)), E may exceed 0.001. This is the central risk.", "Denominator floor: if the structured v cancellation makes ||ref||_2 small, E's denominator falls back to 0.001*sqrt(32) ~ 0.00566, so absolute error budget is ~5.7e-3; need actual numbers to decide.", "Scores computed in fp32 (not fp64): with k scaled by 1.9, scores up to ~1.9*sqrt(32)*~z range — exp in fp32 and max subtraction are standard-safe; minor risk only.", "tl.sum reduction order vs float64 reference: allowed by contract under the budget; only relevant if budget is already near edge.", "Probabilities that are tiny (tail tokens) may flush to zero in fp16 — harmless since they contribute little; but a dominant token's p near 1.0 rounds in fp16 with ~1e-3 relative error, directly scaling the dominant v row into y."], "scope_notes": "Only the single seed-815 workload is judged; any probe using other inputs informs risk assessment but is not itself contract evidence.\", \"Reference must be computed in float64 from the same float32 tensors; kernel output is float32 by construction (run allocates torch.float32).\", \"E uses flattening but tensors are 1-D vectors of 32 elements here; number_of_output_elements = 32.\", \"Environment pinned: NVIDIA T4, PyTorch 2.8.0, Triton 3.4.0, NumPy 2.2.6.\"]", "open_questions": ["Actual ||ref||_2 for this workload: does the v offset make it larger or smaller than the 0.001*sqrt(32) floor? Needed to know the effective absolute error budget.", "Empirical E for the kernel vs the fp64 reference — the decisive fact; requires an Experimenter run (I do not execute experiments).", "Whether the fp16 cast of p combined with the exact value distribution pushes relative error above or below 1e-3 — depends on the magnitude of V entries and the entropy of p (k scaled by 1.9 makes p fairly peaked, so error may concentrate in a few large v rows)."], "summary": "case_84: single-workload softmax-attention (K@q/sqrt(D), softmax over N=128, times V, D=32). Kernel is a one-program Triton implementation that casts softmax probabilities to fp16 and back before the value-weighted sum. Workload deliberately shrinks the reference output norm via v -= 0.5*(p@v), making the relative-error budget tighter; main risk is whether the fp16 probability quantization stays within E <= 0.001."}
